typeomega.birch_world.ui.manual.7: =credit = 2^44 EU x layers x M/M☉  (40 layers a phase)

typeomega.fusion_suppressor.ui.manual.13: Either ending gives a burst of research (2000 or 5000 points). Do it in a system made for it: the star does not come back.
typeomega.fusion_suppressor.ui.manual.14: Repair: idle, put suppressor-ring blocks in an input bus (+5% each).
typeomega.fusion_suppressor.ui.manual.4: Research goes to the owner's GTNA knowledge points, area typeomega:astrophysics.

typeomega.hraemc.ui.manual.1: Matter fed to the disk spirals down to the innermost stable orbit and gives off part of its rest energy as light.

typeomega.hraemc.ui.manual.13: The antennas (phase 5) give log₂(power)/4 research points a second (GTNA knowledge, area typeomega:astrophysics).

typeomega.matrioshka.needs_star: No star here: the Matrioshka Brain only works in the Nexus System.
typeomega.matrioshka.psi: Ψ of the owner: %s thought cycles
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.fracture_warning: %s shell(s) fractured: put their blocks in an input bus
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.limit_hint: Limit now: %s K (the main rings of phase 4 add 40 K).
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.0: The Matrioshka Brain wraps the Nexus star in shells of computers. Each finished phase is one shell, computing with the starlight that reaches it.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.10: Temperatures move slowly (10 s time constant): a short clock peak can be held before the shells heat up.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.11: = T > 500 K (540 K with phase 4) → overheated: no CWU, -2% integrity a second
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.12: An overheated shell computes nothing and wears; the outer field of phase 5 halves the wear. At 0% the shell fractures and stays off.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.13: Repair: put the shell's own blocks in an input bus on the station. Each block gives back 5%, one per shell a second, while it is not overheated.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.14: = Ψ/s = (max CWU/t × 20 - CWU used in the second) / 2^20
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.15: CWU nobody asks for becomes Ψ (thought cycles), kept for the owner like the Nexus network's EU.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.16: Send CWU through up to 2 Optical Data Transmission Hatches on the station; coolant and repair blocks enter through fluid hatches and input buses there too.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.17: The brain only works in the Nexus System, around its star.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.18: Phases 2 to 5 can come later: a phase counts once all its blocks and those of the phases before it are in place.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.19: While it runs, every ring but the polar one leaves the world and turns; switching off puts them back.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.2: A shell at radius r sits in the star's light. Radiating more power (a higher clock) needs a hotter shell.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.3: = CWU/t of shell n = 2^(21+n) × clock × 300 K / T
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.4: Landauer's limit: erasing a bit costs k·T·ln 2, so a colder shell computes more with the same energy. The cold outer shells give the most.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.6: A coolant pulls the shells towards its own temperature Tc. The best one in the fluid hatches is used:
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.7: = He 4 K, η 0.40, 250 mB/s · He-II 2 K, η 0.60, 100 mB/s · DSS 0.1 K, η 0.85, 10 mB/s (per phase, × clock)
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.manual.8: Superfluid helium comes from liquid helium in a Vacuum Freezer; the Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid from the Forge of the Gods' chain.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.no_star: No star here: build it in the Nexus System.
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.overheat_warning: %s shell(s) overheated: lower the clock or add coolant
typeomega.matrioshka.ui.shells_hint: Unbuilt shells show what they would give at this clock and coolant.
typeomega.me_interface.capacity: Each slot holds %sx a stack: up to %s items or %s B of fluid
typeomega.me_interface.upgrade: Sneak right-click a lower-tier interface of the same form to replace it, keeping its config and contents
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.idle.neutronium: Waiting: not enough neutronium dust for a batch
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.idle.no_recipe: Waiting: no alloy recipe matches the buses
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.idle.power: Waiting: not enough EU in the Nexus network
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.1: Neutron-star matter is packed to ~4 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³: a thin layer of neutronium dust under the hammers presses a whole batch at once.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.10: =neutronium per batch = max(1, 2^c / 2) after the pulsar vicinity
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.11: Without enough dust for one batch the forge waits; it never runs a batch it cannot press.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.2: =parallel = 256 × 2^c;  neutronium per batch = 2^c  (compression c from 0 to 4)
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.3: Each built phase opens one more step of compression (c ≤ phases - 1). EU is paid from the Nexus network as in the base recipe.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.5: A neutron star's field reaches 10⁸–10¹¹ T. The superconducting ring (phase 2) rides it, and the press strikes four times as often.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.7: Make one with the Interstellar System Creator, or let the Fusion Suppressor collapse a star of 8-20 M☉.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.9: Once the Stellar Engine has carried the network to the pulsar vicinity, the press arm (phase 3) pulls fresh neutronium from its wind.
typeomega.nidavellir.ui.manual.tip: How the forge works, with its formulas.

typeomega.organ_modifier.tooltip.2: Each organ set gives different effects

typeomega.qso.final_broadcast: The Quasi-Stellar Obliterator fires its last shot. The universe has no order left to give. The game is over.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.1: A quasar is a black hole swallowing matter at its Eddington limit, the brightest steady light there is.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.10: When it is spent, the next shot is the last: the Final era closes and the game ends.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.11: The world holds 100,000 units; what you harvest is kept for the final recipes.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.2: =input = 2^40 EU/t x M/M☉ x 20 + 2^42 EU/s x draw (0-16)
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.3: =charge = charge x 0.99 + input each second;  ceiling = input / 0.01
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.5: A shot of size k holds 2^50 x 2^(k+1) EU; aiming costs 2^50 of it. Sizes up to 2 + phases, at most 7.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.7: Big shots waste less on aiming but fill slowly and leak; past the ceiling they never fire. A heavier hole lifts it.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.9: Ordered energy fired at the 2.7 K sky is negentropy; the world holds only so much, shared by all.
typeomega.qso.ui.manual.tip: How the gun works, with its formulas.
typeomega.speed_card.desc: Each card is worth %s Acceleration Cards
typeomega.speed_card.limit: Shares the machine's Acceleration Card limit with the other tiers; the highest tiers count first
typeomega.speed_card.replace: Sneak right-click a machine at its card limit to replace its lowest-tier card
typeomega.speed_card.scope: Speeds up AE2 and ExtendedAE import/export buses and IO ports
typeomega.star_lifter.needs_star: No star here: the Star Lifter works around the star of a star system.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.girdle_broken: The sphere is broken: repair it with its blocks.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.1: Matter on the star's surface is held by gravity. The lifter heats it and pinches the star's field so it leaves through the poles, where the collector rings catch it.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.11: One second of play is a million years of lifting, so the star really gets lighter.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.12: =ΔM = ṁ × 3.16e13 s per second;  L = M^4;  T = 5772 (L / R²)^¼
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.14: A lighter star is dimmer: the Matrioshka Brain gets (L / L☉)^¾ of its computation, the Stellar Engine pushes a lighter star faster. Below 0.5 M☉ the ring cannot hold the outflow.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.16: The stirring rings (phase 5) stir the core: helium and metals come up and fresh hydrogen goes down, adding to the fuel.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.18: Above 60% the star grows restless: at 100% instability a flare costs the sphere 25%.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.19: Repair: idle, put sphere and spoke blocks in an input bus (+5% each).
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.2: =e = G M / R  (1.9e11 J/kg for the Sun)
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.4: Thermal wind (phase 1) lifts up to 1e11 kg/s; the ring current (phase 2) up to 1e12 kg/s.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.6: The collector rings (phase 3) catch 85% of the outflow; without them only 15% is caught.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.8: Only hydrogen and helium plasma come out until the spires (phase 4) sort oxygen, neon, nitrogen and metal dusts.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.manual.9: Beyond the Orion arm's edge (Stellar Engine) the star's wind is 25% richer.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.no_spires: Phase 4 sorts metals and gases out of the plasma.
typeomega.star_lifter.ui.s.title: The star
typeomega.stellar_engine.needs_star: No star here: the Stellar Engine only works in the Nexus System.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.cage_broken: Cage broken: put rib blocks in an input bus
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.0: The Stellar Engine moves the whole Nexus System. A Shkadov mirror and a Caplan engine work together around its star.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.1: = F(Shkadov) = f × L / c, f = 0.25 (a 60° cap of mirror)
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.10: One second of play is a million years of engine. The Δv gathered is kept for the owner and never goes back.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.11: = Power = 2^36 EU/t from the Nexus network
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.12: Without power only the mirror pushes. The engine also gives hydrogen and helium plasma to the output hatches.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.13: Regions: Orion edge 20 km/s (+25% matter), interarm void 60 (colder Matrioshka shells), emission nebula 120 (more hydrogen), pulsar vicinity 250 (neutronium), galactic core 500.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.14: The galaxy map shows the route, the regions reached and where the system is now.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.15: Phases: 1 cage and station, 2 mirror, 3 collector ring, 4 Caplan engine, 5 nozzle and counter-jet guides.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.2: The mirror sends part of the starlight back: the light leaves only on one side and the system moves (Shkadov, 1987).
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.3: = F(Caplan) = β × ṁ × v_e, v_e = 0.01 c, ṁ = 10^12 kg/s
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.4: The Caplan engine lifts hydrogen and helium from the star with magnetic fields, fuses the helium and fires two jets (Caplan, 2019).
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.5: β is the share of the lifted mass in the main jet; the rest goes back into the star so it follows the engine.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.6: = Tension = (β - 70%) / 20%, at least 50% without the guides of phase 5
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.7: Above 70% the counter-jet cannot hold the star and the cage strains: -2% integrity a second at full tension.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.8: Repair the cage with rib and hoop blocks in an input bus on the station, +5% a block, while there is no tension.
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.manual.9: = Δv per second = F / M_sun × 10^6 years
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.no_power: Caplan engine without EU: only the mirror pushes
typeomega.stellar_engine.ui.no_star: No star here: build it in the Nexus System.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.heat.tip: Core heating: left click +0.05, right click -0.05.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.1: Fusion speeds up steeply with core temperature: as T^4 in the proton-proton chain of light stars, T^16 in the CNO cycle of stars above 1.3 M☉.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.10: A neutron star feeds the Nidavellir, a black hole the HRAE-MC. Make a star for the purpose with the System Creator.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.11: The countdown shows the time left at the present heat; it cannot be undone once the core is gone.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.2: =boost = (1 + h)^n,  n = 4 or 16;  h up to 0.3 x phases
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.3: =power = 2^30 EU/t x L/L☉ x boost  (boost at most a million)
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.5: Only the core hydrogen burns: 0.7% of the mass of a tenth of the star turns into light.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.6: =budget = 2^60 EU x M/M☉ x fuel left
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.7: Heating harder burns the same budget faster: the total never grows. Heavy stars hold more and burn far faster.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.9: When the core is spent the star ends by its mass: below 8 M☉ a white dwarf, to 20 M☉ a neutron star, above a black hole.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.manual.ti: How the harvest works, with its formulas.
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.spent.1: Spent: the star is a white dwarf
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.spent.2: Spent: the core collapsed to a neutron star
typeomega.stellar_harvester.ui.spent.3: Spent: the core collapsed to a black hole
typeomega.stellar_hoop.needs_star: No star here: the Stellar Hoop works around the star of a star system.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.1: An eccentric hoop turns about its own centre; once a turn each segment passes the dive point, just above the photosphere, and its crucibles take in the corona's plasma.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.11: Each mB of liquid helium takes 1 unit of load, Helium II 3, shifted superfluid 10; the best one in the hatches is used.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.13: At 0% the hoop stops. Idle, it takes shield and hull blocks from an input bus: +5% each.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.14: The second hoop (phase 5) runs higher and doubles the crucibles.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.3: Recipes up to that heat run: fusion, Electric Blast Furnace and Plasma Forge.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.6: The corona thins out with height (scale height ~7% R): lower plasma is denser, so more of it comes in at once.
typeomega.stellar_hoop.ui.manual.9: The load rises faster than the parallel: a high dive is cheaper per craft, a low one faster.
typeomega.suprashell.ui.idle.no_recipe: Waiting: no hosted recipe matches the buses
typeomega.suprashell.ui.idle.power: Waiting: not enough EU in the Nexus network
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.1: Put GTCEu multiblock controllers in the input buses: each is a module; the shell runs the recipes of all their kinds.
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.11: Close: cheap and slow, few modules. Far: full price, fast, room for hundreds.
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.2: =parallel = 64 x modules hosted  (up to the room)
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.3: =room = r^2 modules (r in rs), at most 64 x phases
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.5: A static shell near a black hole sits deep in its well: its clocks run slow, seen from outside.
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.7: At 1.5 rs the shell works at 58%; at 20 rs, at 97%.
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.9: Matter lowered on a rope from far away down to the shell gives up 1 - tau of its rest energy (Geroch's process).
typeomega.suprashell.ui.manual.tip: How the shell works, with its formulas.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.cancel.tip: Let the cloud disperse: what was gathered and the Ψ are lost.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.forge.tip: Start a star: takes the Ψ and the iron dust now, then gathers hydrogen from the hatches.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.kind.tip: Click to pick the next star kind (the chart shows heat to the left, light upwards).
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.1: Stars form when a cold cloud collapses under its own gravity. The Creator gathers the cloud, squeezes it with its rings and lights the core with the Fusion Candle.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.10: =E = 2^41 EU × M² / R  (binding energy ∝ (3/5) G M²/R)
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.12: Phase 1 red dwarf (0.3 M☉), 2 yellow dwarf (1), 3 white star (2), 4 blue giant (15), 5 neutron star (from 15 M☉ of gas) and black hole (from 25).
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.13: Remnants need four times the Ψ: the collapse is computed through the lens.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.14: Metallicity Z (½, 1, 2, 3 × the Sun) sets how rich the new system is when mined or taken apart.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.16: Each new star becomes a system of its own (six slots). The orrery picks one; Travel takes you to its landing platform.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.17: =Dimensional era: I at 1 system, II at 3, III at 6
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.18: Stars that are burnt, suppressed or taken apart (Harvester, Fusion Suppressor, Disintegrator) are meant for these systems.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.19: Dispersing a cloud loses what was gathered and the Ψ spent.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.3: =Ψ = 2^20 × M × Z;  iron dust = 16 × M × Z
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.4: Gathering takes up to 50 000 mB a second from the hatches.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.6: The cloud falls in on itself in its free-fall time; a disk forms round the protostar and two jets leave its poles.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.7: =t_ff = √(3π / 32 G ρ) ∝ √(R³/M):  60 s for a Sun, 20 to 300 s
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.9: The Fusion Candle (phase 3) pays the cloud's binding energy over 20 s; without it only a red dwarf lights, slowly and without EU.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.manual.tip: How stars are made here, with the formulas.
typeomega.system_creator.ui.metal.tip: Metallicity of the new system: richer systems give more when mined or taken apart, and cost more Ψ and iron.

typeomega.system_creator.ui.msg.phase: That star needs a later phase

typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.1: Plants buoyed in the gas giant's atmosphere grow from seeds kept in the input bus, like a Greenhouse, by the hundred.
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.10: =z* = 0.5 ln(L / 0.015)  (Sun: 2.1; blue giant: the bottom; red dwarf: the top)
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.11: The chart shows the curve for this star: the gold line is your depth, the dashed one the best.
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.2: =parallel = 256 x phases;  biomass = 100 mB per harvest
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.3: Recipes: the Greenhouse. EU comes from the Nexus network, as in the base recipe.
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.5: Sunlight fades as the gardens sink (Beer-Lambert), while the pressure and the carbon dioxide grow (barometric).
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.6: =I = L e^-z;  c = 0.05 e^z;  growth = I/(I + 0.3) x c/(c + 1)
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.7: Depth z is in scale heights, 0 to 8; L is the star's luminosity in suns. Rate = 10 x growth, from x0.05 to x6.
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.9: Growth peaks where light and carbon limit it equally: deeper round a bright star, near the top round a dim one.
typeomega.yggdrasil.ui.manual.tip: How the gardens grow, with the formulas.
